# Femoral neck abnormalities

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Trauma and orthopedic surgery > Lower extremity > Femoral neck abnormalities*

[Original Article Link](/library/lQ0vwf)

---

## Summary

Femoral neck abnormalities are axial malalignments of the femoral neck involving the caput-collum-diaphyseal angle and the <u>femoral angle of anteversion</u>. Four common femoral version abnormalities are discussed here: <u>coxa vara</u>, <u>coxa valga</u>, <u>femoral anteversion</u>, and <u>femoral retroversion</u>. Clinical features include an abnormal gait and <u>pain</u> with prolonged <u>weight-bearing</u>. Some abnormalities may resolve spontaneously. However, severe cases require surgical correction. Common complications include secondary arthrosis and <u>femoroacetabular impingement</u>.
